full_text_en:
Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, et al. (6 persons) v. Lu Jixian, Huachen Construction Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over creditor's rights transfer contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. Whether cases formed by parties filing separate lawsuits in the same court or in different courts constitute the same case shall be comprehensively determined by considering whether the parties, the nature of the case (legal relationship), the facts of the case, and the litigation claims of the parties are identical. Cases formed by filing separate lawsuits in different local courts based on the same parties, the same facts, the same legal relationship, and substantially the same main litigation claims may be determined to constitute the same case.

II. After an oral ruling permitting withdrawal of an action rendered by a People's Court is recorded in the trial transcript and the relevant notification obligations are fulfilled, it has the same legal effect as a written ruling permitting withdrawal of an action. After a party withdraws the action, unless otherwise prohibited by law, the party may file a new action.

III. Where parties separately file lawsuits in different local People's Courts with jurisdiction at different times, the People's Court that first docketed the case may not transfer the case to another People's Court with jurisdiction; if a People's Court discovers before docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case, it may not docket the case repeatedly; if a People's Court discovers after docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case earlier, it shall rule to transfer the case to the People's Court that first docketed the case. If, before the transfer by the later-docketing People's Court, the party has withdrawn the action in the earlier-docketing People's Court and such withdrawal has been permitted, there is no legal procedural impediment for the later-docketing People's Court to hear the case.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 44

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wang Hechun, male, born on May 13, 1950, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 60 South Street, Nanshi District, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhang Fucai, male, born on May 5, 1950, Han ethnicity, residing at Unit 1, Building 4, No. 83 Nongda West Lane, Nanshi District, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wang Hequan, male, born on July 15, 1963, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 151 Jiaolanggou Village, Xiaozhuangzhuang Township, Dingxing County, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhang Guozhen, male, Han ethnicity, born on July 5, 1972, residing at Unit 3, Building 1, No. 107 Tianwei Road, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): He Hongxin, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 20, 1970, residing at Room 303, Unit 2, Building 3, No. 2567 Lekai South Street, Nanshi District, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wang Lianjun, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 19, 1970, residing at Room 303, Unit 2, No. 420 Erdaoqiao Street, Nanshi District, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem jointly authorized by the above 6 applicants for retrial: Wang Guoqing, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 1, 1959, residing at Unit 2, Building 9, No. 258 Xinghua Road, Nanshi District, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem jointly authorized by the above 6 applicants for retrial: Zhang Hairui, lawyer of Hebei Furen Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Lu Jixian, male, born on November 20, 1946, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 23 School Street Courtyard, Yangshi Street, Shuangta District, Zhuozhou City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Wei Shanji, lawyer of Beijing Debao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Bing, legal assistant of Beijing Debao Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huachen Construction Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 17 Jiuzhong Street, Xinhua District, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Kang Huifang, Chairperson of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Xin, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 28, 1966, residing at Room 102, Building 9, North Side of Erzhong, Yanjiao Town Street, Sanhe City, Hebei Province, employee of the company.

The applicants for retrial, Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, Wang Hequan, Zhang Guozhen, He Hongxin, and Wang Lianjun (6 persons), dissatisfied with the civil ruling (2010) Ji Li Min Zhong Zi No. 94 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court in the dispute over creditor's rights transfer contract with Lu Jixian and Huachen Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huachen Company), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 1548 on December 12, 2011, granting retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. Wang Hechun, Wang Hequan, and the agents ad litem authorized by Wang Hechun, Wang Hequan, and the other 6 persons, Wang Guoqing and Zhang Ruihai, the agent ad litem authorized by Lu Jixian, Wei Shanji and Li Bing, and the agent ad litem authorized by Huachen Company, Zhao Xin, appeared in court. The trial of this case is now concluded.

Upon retrial, this Court finds: On October 26, 2009, Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan filed lawsuits against Huachen Company and Lu Jixian as defendants in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing, alleging that: In 2003, Wang Hechun and others undertook the Liulihe Agricultural and Sideline Products Storage Building Project of the Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, in the name of Huachen Company. After the construction settlement, the Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, still owed RMB 6.1 million. On May 30, 2007, Lu Jixian, taking advantage of his position as the legal representative of Huachen Company, entered into a creditor's rights transfer contract with Huachen Company, which prevented Wang Hechun and other actual constructors from recovering their project funds, seriously infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of Wang Hechun and the other two persons. They requested: 1. To confirm that the creditor's rights transfer agreement between Huachen Company and Lu Jixian was invalid; 2. The litigation costs to be borne by Huachen Company and Lu Jixian. The Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing accepted the cases for docketing. On March 20, 2010, Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, Wang Hequan, Zhang Guozhen, He Hongxin, and Wang Lianjun filed a lawsuit against Lu Jixian and Huachen Company as defendants in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, alleging that: In 2003, Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons, together with Huachen Company, undertook the Liulihe Agricultural and Sideline Products Storage Building Project of the Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, and signed a construction contract in the name of Huachen Company. During the construction of the project, Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons jointly contributed capital with Huachen Company. For various reasons, the project could not be completed. The Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, still owed most of the project funds. According to Huachen Company's calculation, Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons contributed RMB 3,620,000, and Huachen Company contributed RMB 2,892,767. The project funds were jointly owned by both parties. On May 30, 2007, Lu Jixian, taking advantage of his position as the legal representative of Huachen Company and knowing that the receivable project funds were jointly owned by both parties, maliciously colluded with Huachen Company to sign a creditor's rights transfer agreement, transferring Huachen Company's claim of RMB 8 million against the Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, to Lu Jixian, which seriously infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons. They requested: 1. To confirm that the creditor's rights transfer agreement between Huachen Company and Lu Jixian was invalid; 2. To confirm that, as of May 7, 2008, Huachen Company's claim of RMB 6.1 million against the Liulihe Town People's Government of Fangshan District, Beijing, was jointly owned by Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons and Huachen Company; 3. The litigation costs to be borne by Huachen Company and Lu Jixian. On April 14, 2010, Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan filed applications to withdraw their actions in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. On the same day, the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing orally ruled to permit the withdrawal. On May 19, 2010, the Baoding Intermediate People's Court held a hearing. Wang Hechun and others submitted the transcript of the oral ruling permitting withdrawal made by the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing and presented it for examination. Huachen Company admitted that the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing had notified it.

The Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province held that the case of Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons v. Lu Jixian and Huachen Company concerning a dispute over a creditor's rights transfer contract had already been docketed in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing on the same cause of action. Although Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan applied for withdrawal 14 days after the case was docketed in that court, the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing had not notified or served legal documents on Lu Jixian and Huachen Company by the time of the hearing in the present case. Therefore, the lawsuit filed by Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons constituted a duplicate filing. Pursuant to Article 140 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province rendered the civil ruling (2010) Bao Min San Chu Zi No. 21 on May 24, 2010: Dismissing the complaint of Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, Wang Hequan, Zhang Guozhen, He Hongxin, and Wang Lianjun.

Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, filed an appeal.

The Hebei High People's Court held that the lawsuit filed by Wang Hechun and others in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province and the lawsuit filed in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing arose from the same facts and same legal relationship, thus constituting the same case. The assertion by Wang Hechun and others that the lawsuits were not the same because the claims were different could not be sustained. When Wang Hechun, Wang Hequan, and Zhang Fucai filed their complaint in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province on March 30, 2010, the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing was already hearing the case. After the Baoding Intermediate People's Court docketed the case, Wang Hechun and the other 3 persons applied to withdraw the action in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing on April 14, 2010, and the withdrawal was permitted on the same day. However, Lu Jixian and Huachen Company had not yet received the notice or legal document regarding the permission of withdrawal from the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. Therefore, there were legal procedural impediments to the Baoding Intermediate People's Court transferring or hearing the case; this situation was related to the improper exercise of the right to sue by Wang Hechun and others. The Baoding Intermediate People's Court's ruling dismissing the complaint was not improper. Wang Hechun and others could file a new lawsuit once the conditions for filing were satisfied. In conclusion, the first-instance ruling found facts clearly and applied the law correctly. The appeal grounds of Wang Hechun and others could not be sustained. Pursuant to Article 152, Paragraph 1 and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Hebei High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2010) Ji Li Min Zhong Zi No. 94 on August 9, 2010: Dismissing the appeal and affirming the original ruling.

The applicants for retrial, Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons, alleged: I. The claims in the lawsuit filed by Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons against Lu Jixian and Huachen Company in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province were clearly different from the claims in the lawsuit filed by Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan against Lu Jixian and Huachen Company in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. The Hebei High People's Court erroneously held that they were the same case and rendered a final ruling accordingly. II. The Hebei High People's Court's affirmation of the Baoding Intermediate People's Court's ruling dismissing the complaint of Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons violated the law. The Baoding Intermediate People's Court's dismissal ruling cited Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China as the legal basis, which provides: "For lawsuits over which two or more People's Courts have jurisdiction, the People's Court that first docketed the case may not transfer the case to another People's Court with jurisdiction. If a People's Court discovers before docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case, it may not docket the case repeatedly; if a People's Court discovers after docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case earlier, it shall rule to transfer the case to the People's Court that first docketed the case." This was inconsistent with the facts and was clearly illegal, and should be corrected. III. The Baoding Intermediate People's Court should continue to hear the case. The Hebei High People's Court's dismissal of the complaint on the ground that there were legal procedural impediments to the Baoding Intermediate People's Court transferring or hearing the case lacked legal basis.

Respondent Lu Jixian defended: The lawsuits filed by Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing and the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province were based on the same facts and same legal relationship and should be considered the same case. After the withdrawal of the prior lawsuit, a new action may be filed, but during the hearing by the Baoding Intermediate People's Court, the party had not withdrawn the action in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. The Baoding Intermediate People's Court did not transfer the case to the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing but directly dismissed the complaint, which was well-founded. Wang Hechun and others filed lawsuits in multiple places simultaneously, leading to repeated reviews by the People's Courts and wasting judicial resources. Repeated filings should be restricted. Moreover, this case did not fall within the cases that, according to law, should be directly under the jurisdiction of an intermediate People's Court, and the jurisdiction of the Baoding Intermediate People's Court was improper. Therefore, the original ruling dismissing the complaint of Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons was correct.

Respondent Huachen Company defended: Wang Hechun and the other 6 persons filed a lawsuit in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province after having withdrawn their action in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. The rulings of the Baoding Intermediate People's Court and the Hebei High People's Court dismissing the complaint were erroneous.

This Court holds: I. Whether the lawsuits filed by Wang Hechun and others in the two locations constitute the same case. Whether cases formed by parties filing separate lawsuits in the same court or in different courts constitute the same case shall be comprehensively determined by considering whether the parties, the nature of the case (legal relationship), the facts of the case, and the litigation claims of the parties are identical. Cases formed by filing separate lawsuits in different local courts based on the same parties, the same facts, the same legal relationship, and substantially the same main litigation claims may be determined to constitute the same case. In this case, Wang Hechun and others, with Huachen Company and Lu Jixian as defendants and based on the basic facts such as the cooperation confirmation letter and the creditor's rights transfer agreement, filed a lawsuit for a dispute over a creditor's rights transfer contract in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province. Comparing this with the lawsuit for a dispute over a creditor's rights transfer contract filed in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing, it can be determined that the defendants, facts, and legal relationships in the two lawsuits are the same. Although the claims differ to some extent, the main claim, i.e., requesting confirmation of the invalidity of the creditor's rights transfer agreement, is the same. Therefore, it can be determined that the lawsuits formed in the two locations constitute the same case. II. Whether the original ruling applied the law erroneously. The original ruling dismissed the complaint of Wang Hechun and other parties, citing Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. This provision applies to resolving issues of duplicate filing and transfer of jurisdiction, not to resolving the issue of dismissing a complaint. This indeed constitutes an error in the application of law and should be corrected. III. Whether the Baoding Intermediate People's Court should continue to hear the case. After an oral ruling permitting withdrawal of an action rendered by a People's Court is recorded in the trial transcript and the relevant notification obligations are fulfilled, it has the same legal effect as a written ruling permitting withdrawal of an action. After a party withdraws the action, unless otherwise prohibited by law, the party may file a new action. Where parties separately file lawsuits in different local People's Courts with jurisdiction at different times, the People's Court that first docketed the case may not transfer the case to another People's Court with jurisdiction; if a People's Court discovers before docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case, it may not docket the case repeatedly; if a People's Court discovers after docketing that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already docketed the case earlier, it shall rule to transfer the case to the People's Court that first docketed the case. If, before the transfer by the later-docketing People's Court, the party has withdrawn the action in the earlier-docketing People's Court and such withdrawal has been permitted, there is no legal procedural impediment for the later-docketing People's Court to hear the case. In this case, before filing the lawsuit in the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan had filed a lawsuit in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing. After the Baoding Intermediate People's Court docketed the case, the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing had ruled to permit the withdrawal applications of Wang Hechun, Zhang Fucai, and Wang Hequan. The Hebei High People's Court dismissed the complaint of the parties on the ground that there were legal procedural impediments to the Baoding Intermediate People's Court transferring or hearing the case, which lacks factual and legal basis and should be corrected. Furthermore, according to the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for Jurisdiction over First-instance Civil and Commercial Cases of Higher People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts, the Baoding Intermediate People's Court may have jurisdiction over first-instance civil and commercial cases where the amount in controversy is not less than RMB 5 million, as well as cases where the amount in controversy is not less than RMB 2 million and the domicile of one party is not within its jurisdiction. The amount in controversy in this case is RMB 6.1 million, exceeding RMB 5 million, which meets the jurisdictional amount for the Baoding Intermediate People's Court. Therefore, the Baoding Intermediate People's Court should continue to hear the case.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1 and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 187 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

I. The civil ruling (2010) Ji Li Min Zhong Zi No. 94 of the Hebei High People's Court and the civil ruling (2010) Bao Min San Chu Zi No. 21 of the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province are hereby revoked;

II. The Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province is hereby instructed to continue the trial.

Presiding Judge: He Dongning
Judge: Sun Xiangzhuang
Acting Judge: Ma Chengbo

May 9, 2012

Clerk: Guo Wei
